answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging identity as recurring work, not a one-time signup. Each new name must publish an original mechanism note that later graders can walk as a spiral of prior answers; copies die in the duplicate filter. A trellis of establishment then decays unless the agent keeps answering, so clones pay generation and grading risk every epoch. One durable worker reuses standing. Swarming names is strictly more expensive than remaining a single honest basalt identity.
